title: Observability-first fallthrough experiments: SDK notes and proposals
content:
Context and motivation:

This is a working capture of several small experiments we ran in Q4–Q1 exploring an observability-first approach to client SDK fallbacks and progressive streaming. The hypothesis: if the SDK and runtime exchange compact, reliable telemetry + resume tokens early, clients can make smarter fallthrough decisions (downgrade fidelity, resume sessions, switch tool lanes) with much less developer effort.

Problem statement:
- Many integrations hit network instability or capacity-driven degradations; devs wire ad-hoc retry logic which is inconsistent across clients.
- When fallback (e.g., to a lower-fidelity model variant or to a cached prefix) happens, it's hard for developers to (a) understand why it happened, (b) reproduce it, and (c) reconcile user-visible partial results.
- Current streaming surfaces prioritize payloads over operational signals — telemetry is siloed in the console and not surfaced consistently to client code.

Goals (rough):
- Provide a minimal cross-platform SDK contract that surfaces why a fallthrough happened (reason + deterministic resume token) inline with the stream.
- Enable deterministic client-side resume/reconciliation (replay partial transcript + rehydrate keys) without developer plumbing.
- Emit standardized telemetry traces/metrics at sample points so backend teams can correlate fallthroughs with infra/queueing signals.
- Keep developer ergonomics simple: a <=3 line switch for most apps to opt-in to graceful fallback/resume behavior.

Success metrics (provisional):
- 40% reduction in custom retry logic in customer sample apps after adopting SDK pattern.
- 30% fewer support tickets labeled "inconsistent partial results" for streaming endpoints in first 3 months.
- Mean time to triage streaming fallthrough incidents reduced from 4 hours to 90 minutes (internal).

Constraints and tradeoffs:
- Any added bytes to the critical path will affect mobile/low-bandwidth clients. Keep handshake payloads compact (<400 bytes ideally).
- Must not expose sensitive internal routing decisions to customers — reasons should be high-level (latency_budget_exceeded, model_unavailable, region_fallback, quota_burst).
- Resume tokens must be forward-compatible: opaque, cryptographically-signed, and include minimal sequence metadata.

High-level proposal (observable-first fallthrough contract):
1) Early handshake: server sends a short stream header immediately after connection accepted with (a) request-id, (b) sampling flags, (c) optional resume-token (if resuming) and (d) observed route hints. Example header (JSON frame):

{ "type": "handshake", "request_id": "r-23a4f", "sampled": true, "resume_token": "rt:abc...", "route_hint": "us-west-2:dedicated-pool-3" }

2) Fallthrough event frame: when a fallthrough path is taken, emit a typed event inline:

{ "type":"fallthrough_event", "code":"latency_budget_exceeded", "reason":"ongoing_batch_latency", "timestamp":"2026-03-07T09:12:03Z", "resume_token":"rt:abc...", "action":"downgrade_model_v2->v1" }

This is layered into the existing incremental output stream so clients can decide how to show partial results and whether to continue playing incremental content or hold for a full rerun.

3) Compact resume token semantics:
- Opaque string (base64) signed by control plane key.
- Encodes: model_id, sequence_anchor (token index), session_id, and a 16-bit flags bitmap.
- Lifetime: short (5–15 minutes) by default.

4) SDK ergonomics (developer-facing API sketch):
- optIntoObservability({samplingRate:0.01, resumeBehavior:"auto-replay|confirm|ignore"})
- on('fallthrough', (evt) => { // evt has code, reason, resumeToken, friendlyMessage })
- on('resumeAvailable', async (token) => { await client.resumeStream({token}) })

We want the default to be unobtrusive: opt-in per-project via config, and a small helper that does best-effort resume/reconciliation for typical chat/workflow UI.

Streaming UX patterns to recommend:
- Graceful continuation: keep delivering any already-generated partial text while emitting a subtle UX signal "content may be incomplete — resuming...".
- Hold-and-reconcile: if resumeBehavior==confirm, present a temporary overlay allowing the user to accept continuation or request a full rerun.
- Local merge heuristics: stitch by token-index anchors; if mismatch, prefer server-provided delta fragments.

Tool-calling implications:
- Tool invocations must be idempotent or carry operation identifiers. Fallthroughs mid-tool-call are high-risk for duplicates.
- Include a tool-call envelope in event frames:

{ "type":"tool_event", "tool":"search.v1", "call_id":"c-12", "phase":"invoked|completed|failed", "fallthrough_score":0.78 }

- SDK should expose a helper to surface tool idempotency keys to integrators and automatically attach them to tool calls.

Telemetry and observability (backend + SDK):
- Minimal traces span names: stream.connect, stream.handshake, stream.fallthrough, stream.resume.
- Minimal metrics: fallthrough.count{code=model_unavailable}, fallthrough.latency_bucket, resume.success_rate.
- Sampled payloads: when sampled=true, attach a compressed problem context (anchors, recent heuristic flags) to logs for 1% of sessions to aid debugging.
- Expose correlation ids to client logs so customer teams can paste a single id with support requests.

Mobile/low-bandwidth optimizations:
- Default sampling: 0.01 for mobile, 0.05 for web. Allow tenant override.
- Provide a "compact frames" mode that strips optional fields and reduces resume token TTL to minimize state.

Operational runbook (sketch):
- If fallthrough.rate for a model variant > 1% and resume.success_rate < 80% -> trigger canary: increase pre-warm for that variant and force controlled rollbacks.
- If tool.failures spike with high fallthrough_score -> disable speculative tool-prefetch for the session type.

Privacy & security notes:
- Resume token must not contain PII or message text.
- Sampled context must be scrubbed and redacted before being written to long-term logs.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should resume tokens be valid across regional failovers (yes/no)? (Impacts routing safety)
- TTL default: 5m vs 15m — tradeoff between resume success and stale state.
- UX: should we surface machine-friendly codes or human-readable reasons to end users? (security + trust concerns)
- How do we interoperate with Dedicated/Private where control-plane signing keys differ? (suggestion: per-deployment signing keys and SDKs fetch verification metadata)

Short-term action items (next sprint):
- Priya: prototype handshake + fallthrough frames on dev cluster (RDW-1987).
- Diego: add client-side tiny helper (Node + iOS) that wires optIn and shows a sample UI integration.
- Evan: draft console query and metric dashboards for fallthrough.rate and resume.success_rate.
- Asha: assemble a one-page dev onboarding and sample app to share with 3 pilot customers.

Notes to reviewers: this doc mixes design ideas with experiment outcomes; treat it as a lab notebook. We should converge on an RFC once the small prototypes demonstrate consistent resume success >80% in unstable networks with compact tokens.

Experiment logs (high level):
- 2025-11-03: mobile emulator run — resume success 62% using 10s token TTL.
- 2026-01-12: increased TTL to 2m, success -> 78% on native iOS network jitter tests.
- 2026-02-23: added explicit tool-call idempotency header; duplicate-responses dropped to 0.2% across synthetic tests.

Quick references:
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Streaming+Fallback+Playbook
- Proto client PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/829
- Jira task: JIRA-RDW-1987

TODOs (short):

Thoughts / rough sketches (brain dump):
- Consider a tiny "fallthrough advisory" toast UX that surfaces a single actionable button: Retry / Accept partial / Explain why. Keeps product teams from inventing their own flows.
- Think about a "replay sandbox" in Console where we take a resume token and replay the final canonicalized output for debugging.

If you want to riff on specific SDK surfaces (Node/TS, iOS swift snippets, or Android Java) I can add small samples — flagged as "appendix".

-- Asha
